source: Boiro MY 2020 doctoral dissertation abstract (avtoreferat) Comprehensive assessment of the epidemiological situation in Guinea, CNIIE Moscow - Table 2 cholera 1970-2014
processing_notes: Source states: 'Boiro 2020 avtoreferat p.24, Table 2 'Холера в Гвинее: заболеваемость и летальность в 1970-2014 гг.' row '2002 1361 142 10,4' (Cholera in Guinea: morbidity and mortality 1970-2014 - 2002: 1,361 cases, 142 deaths, CFR 10.4%); second, independent channel IFRC Information Bulletin 1/2004 (17 Aug 2004, meta 29) citing the Ministry of Health: 'Between 2002 and 2003, 1,361 cases were recorded with 142 deaths.'' - interpreted as 1361 sCh cases, 142 deaths. Interpreted as 1,361 sCh / 142 deaths, national MoH total for the 2002-2003 epidemic. Period set to 2002-01-01..2003-12-31 because IFRC dates the figure 'between 2002 and 2003' while Boiro's outbreak-year table books it under 2002 and has no 2003 line (the SAP database nonetheless holds ~116 cases in 2003: Conakry, Coyah, Kindia, Dubreka, Lola - AI rows from Sudre 2009 Fig. 6), so the figure most likely spans the 2002-2003 season. Two-year aggregate. CONFLICT: WHO notifications 2002 61 cases/11 deaths (JHU WHO-annual UID 317; AI rows 278, 279, 282 = WER Sep-Dec 2002 notifications) + 2003 6/1 = 67/12, about 1/20 of the MoH figure -> WHO under-notification of the 2002 epidemic (same pattern as 1978 and 1986). Confidence lowered to 0.6 (forced below the Level-2 band) for the WHO conflict and the period ambiguity. JHU outranks AI in the weekly builder for 2002-2003, so this row documents the MoH figure without entering the national weekly series. Same lead author as Boiro 1999/2016 (meta 157, 25); IFRC 2004 is a separate publication channel of the MoH statistic, which satisfies the >1000 second-source rule. Not double-counted with the WER partial notifications: national total, do not sum with rows 278, 279, 282, 283.

source: Het Parool (Amsterdam) 20 Aug 1970 'Vermoedelijk uitbarsting van cholera in Guinee' (WHO Geneva statement of 19 Aug 1970; Delpher)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Het Parool, 20 Aug 1970: 'Een geheimzinnige ziekte, waarschijnlijk cholera, heeft in de Westafrikaanse staat Guinee aan 27 mensen het leven gekost, terwijl 230 anderen in het ziekenhuis moesten worden opgenomen, zo heeft de wereldgezondheidsorganisatie (WHO) gisteren in Genève bekendgemaakt. De WHO deelde mede dat de slachtoffers allen aan "ernstige diarrhee" leden' (A mysterious disease, probably cholera, has killed 27 people in Guinea while 230 others had to be hospitalised, WHO announced in Geneva yesterday; all victims suffered from severe diarrhoea).' - interpreted as 257 sCh cases, 27 deaths. Suspected cholera (not yet laboratory-confirmed at the time; El Tor Ogawa later identified). Early-epidemic snapshot - do not sum with the 1970 national rows: AI row 318 (MoH 6,378/150, Jul-Aug 1970), JHU WHO 1970 2,000/60, AI row 345 (Conakry 2,000/60 to 4 Sep).
